This comparison details patient characteristics for individuals treated for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and related conditions across Denmark's five administrative regions during the period from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023 [^src1]. Because the data represents a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established from this table alone [^src1]. Furthermore, the dataset does not define specific performance targets or thresholds, meaning no standardized goals can be evaluated as met or missed [^src1].

[[Region Hovedstaden]] is the clear leader in total patient volume, managing 11,211 patients, which accounts for the highest absolute numbers across nearly all diagnostic categories, including 4,521 patients with [[DK50* Crohns sygdom]] and 6,534 with [[DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]] [^src1]. Conversely, [[Region Nordjylland]] acts as the trailer in overall volume, treating 3,572 patients in total [^src1]. However, when evaluating the proportional distribution of diagnoses, [[Region Nordjylland]] leads in the share of ulcerative colitis cases, which make up 60% of its patient cohort, while [[Region Sjælland]] has the highest proportion of Crohn's disease patients at 45% [^src1]. Rare conditions such as [[DK830F Primær skleroserende kolangitis]] and [[DK912B Korttarmssyndrom]] represent a negligible fraction of the total population across all regions, though [[Region Midtjylland]] records the highest absolute number of short bowel syndrome cases with 34 patients [^src1].

Demographically, the patient population is highly consistent across the country. Women comprise a slight majority, ranging from 53% to 54% in all regions [^src1]. The median age hovers between 46 and 51 years, with [[Region Sjælland]] and [[Region Nordjylland]] having the oldest median patient age at 51 and 50 years, respectively, while [[Region Hovedstaden]] and [[Region Midtjylland]] share the youngest median age of 46 years [^src1]. The most prominent age demographic across all regions is the 30-59 age bracket, whereas patients aged 90 or older constitute an outlier group, representing 0% (rounded) of the population in every region [^src1].

Regarding healthcare delivery methods, [[Region Sjælland]] leads in the proportion of physical consultations, with 69% of its contacts being in-person, while [[Region Nordjylland]] relies most heavily on virtual consultations, which account for 40% of its contact types [^src1]. In absolute terms, [[Region Hovedstaden]] conducted the most physical visits (37,039) and virtual visits (20,516) [^src1].

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner patientkarakteristika — herunder diagnosefordeling, køn, alder, aldersgrupper og kontakttype — for IBD-patienter fordelt på de fem regioner i perioden 1/10/2022–30/09/2023, og viser en dominerende andel af voksne kvinder med ulcerøs colitis samt en relativt ensartet aldersfordeling.
